title: science entity observation mixin
$comment: Field set frozen by docs/plans/2026-07-30-schema-closure-observation-slice-inventory.md over 21 authored records, ALL in ~/d/health/processes/cycles -- the only single-project-root kind in the tranche, so its corpus can vary nothing and almost nothing here is decided by measuring it. Two omissions are decisions rather than absences: `profile` (0 of 21 authored, 0 of that project's 539 entity records authored, and NOT injected -- see the correction in the inventory doc) and `consolidated_into` (written onto a member's frontmatter by consolidate.py:183 and restored to a live path by unarchive; ruled a writer defect and fixed there, since the archive index is the only thing that reads it).

id.$comment: PREFIX only, per the ruling in mixin-hypothesis-2.0: base 2.0 owns the id's shape and the mixin owns its identity. All 21 ids also satisfy `^observation:[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$`, matching the descriptor's `strategy="slug"` -- measured, not assumed -- and that is still not a reason to pin the slug here; the ruling is about the ids nobody has written yet.

status.$comment: NO enum. The descriptor (profiles/core.py:150) declares [active, retired, archived], but `observation` is not in _CERTIFIED_KINDS (validate/kind_severity.py:24), and status_vocabulary.py rules that an uncertified instrument may not fail anyone's build -- a schema enum fails it HARDER than a validate ERROR, refusing the record at load with no warning stage. Independently, status_vocabulary.py:20-22 rules there is deliberately no second per-kind vocabulary table because the two would drift; a JSON enum here is exactly that table, versioned on a different axis. All 21 records are `active`, which is precisely the uniform-corpus condition that let mixin-concept-1.0's premature enum survive its own certification -- so the corpus is not consulted for this field. REQUIRED, though: templates/observation.md prescribes `status`, so a record without one is a record the toolkit never produces.
